about: Rides into a castle or town of your realm or an ally to cash in. In a town he sells his loot, as far as the town's purse goes: weapons, armour, shields, ammunition, harness and plunder, never food, horses, pack animals, herds, books or banners. A castle buys no loot: only a town does. In a castle or a town he hands his prisoners over in two goes: his captured soldiers first, for their ransom (a castle pays for them as a town does: the price is the man's, not the place's), then his captured enemy lords, who go into its dungeon: in a holding of your own realm for no ransom (the game's rule: it keeps them out of the war and earns his clan a little influence), in the holding of an ally at war with their realm for their ransom. The gold goes into his own purse. Then he is free, or starts his next order. A lord holding any of your orders cashes in the same way whenever he rides into a friendly town (loot and prisoners) or castle (prisoners); this order sends him to do it now.
calls_back: it has cashed in, with what it got
